title: 星天要招实习生  (Xingtian Wants an Intern)

segments.t: Television producer Wang Er arrives on campus looking for Professor Fang. After getting directions from Bu Xiaogu, he surprises Fang by asking for an intern to work on Twelve Singers at Xingtian Entertainment. Listen first.
你好，小同学。
我想问一下，方教授在哪办公啊？
在那边，要不我带您过去？
那太好了，谢谢啊！
老方，这批学生有没有好的？
星天要招实习生？新鲜啊！
他的习惯是不带实习生的。
我跟他不一样，我要了一个实习生的名额。
跟着我，肯定是上十二歌王了。
Let's look closely at each line. Wang Er stops Xiaogu on the campus path with a friendly greeting.
你好，小同学。
'Hello, young student.' Putting "xiao", 'little', in front of "tongxue", 'schoolmate' or 'student', is an affectionate way for an older visitor on campus to greet a student.
我想问一下，方教授在哪办公啊？

'May I ask where Professor Fang has his office?' Starting with "wo xiang wen yixia", literally 'I want to ask once', is a polite cushion before asking a stranger for directions, and "zai na" means 'where'.
在那边，要不我带您过去？
'Over there — how about I take you over?' Notice two polite touches from Xiaogu: "yaobu" offers 'how about...', and she switches from casual "ni" to respectful "nin" for an older guest.
那太好了，谢谢啊！
'That would be wonderful, thank you!' Framing an adjective inside "tai... le" gives you "tai hao le", 'so good!' or 'wonderful!', one of the most natural reactions in spoken Mandarin.
老方，这批学生有没有好的？

'Old Fang, are there any good ones in this batch of students?' Close friends of the same generation put "lao", 'old', before a surname like "Lao Fang", while "you meiyou" asks 'are there or aren't there?'.
星天要招实习生？新鲜啊！
'Xingtian wants to recruit an intern? Now that is something new!' Usually "xinxian" describes fresh fruit or food, so calling news "xinxian" wryly remarks that it is unheard-of.
他的习惯是不带实习生的。
'His habit is never taking on interns.' In workplace Mandarin "dai", 'lead' or 'bring along', also means mentor a newcomer — so "bu dai shixisheng" means refusing to mentor interns.
我跟他不一样，我要了一个实习生的名额。
'I am different from him; I asked for one intern spot.' Remember the pattern "A gen B bu yiyang": "gen" links the two people being compared, and "bu yiyang" says 'not the same'.
跟着我，肯定是上十二歌王了。

'Working under me, it will definitely be on Twelve Singers.' Literally "genzhe wo" says 'following me', which is how Chinese producers talk about working on someone's team. Now listen to the whole campus scene once more.
你好，小同学。
我想问一下，方教授在哪办公啊？
在那边，要不我带您过去？
那太好了，谢谢啊！
老方，这批学生有没有好的？
星天要招实习生？新鲜啊！
他的习惯是不带实习生的。
我跟他不一样，我要了一个实习生的名额。
跟着我，肯定是上十二歌王了。
One coveted intern spot on Twelve Singers is suddenly open, and Xiaogu will not let it slip past. You heard how to ask directions politely with "wo xiang wen yixia" and exclaim "tai hao le".
回头见！
